decision: All 11,836,444 eligible original rows were tokenized without truncation on CPU. Mean question length 46.58, mean program length 73.76, including EOS. Current 128/192 limits cut 19,870 questions and 212,045 programs; 228,035 rows (1.927%) lose some text. 192/384 limits would reduce affected rows to 1,551 (0.013%). This is a corpus census, not proof of checkpoint training exposure or improved accuracy.
next: Keep current production limits until isolated short quality and throughput comparisons. Test a larger output limit separately from a larger input limit, retaining original targets, exact row coverage and strict greedy decoding. No full-pass training or scaling begins from this audit alone.
tests: Three focused synthetic CPU tests passed: quantiles, excluded-row/cap accounting plus verified resume, non-string rejection.

target_damage_sample.scope: Equal-sized per-shard sample of original eligible targets longer than 192 tokens; not a population-weighted estimate.
